text:
marie: Onboarding note: polyglot-embed-v1 (768d) quantized to onnx int6-pertensor. Running multilingual sanity across en/es/zh/pt slices. Seeing larger recall regressions on zh and pt (~3-4% @10) vs en (~0.8%). Anyone seen language-specific sensitivity to quant? :earth_asia:

leo: language differences often reflect tokenization/distributional shifts. Which eval sets?

marie: sampled-news-12m stratified by lang (en,es,zh,pt). Command:

```
python eval_multilang.py \
  --model polyglot-v1 \
  --quant onnx-int6 \
  --calib none \
  --slices en,es,zh,pt \
  --metrics recall@1,5,10,centroid_shift,cosine_tail
```

Baseline fp16 vs int6 aggregated:
- fp16 @10: en=0.801, es=0.787, zh=0.743, pt=0.768
- int6 @10: en=0.794, es=0.772, zh=0.709, pt=0.733
- centroid_shift (avg L2): fp16=0.010, int6=0.017 (zh/pt worst)

anya: did you try per-channel calibration? Also verify tokenizers identical between runs.

marie: tokenizers are same. Spun int6-perchannel calibration on stratified sample (20k per lang). queued job #12011.

mlbot: eval-bot: job 12011 queued by marie (int6-perchannel calibrate).

leo: also check embedding norm distributions by language. Quant can squeeze certain dimensions more if vocab distribution differs. Plot hist per-dim std across langs.

marie: quick diagnostics: zh embeddings have slightly higher variance on dims [120..160], and int6 per-tensor tended to clip those dims. Per-channel calibration reduced clipping. Results from job 12011 (interim):
- int6-perchannel @10: en=0.796, es=0.780, zh=0.723, pt=0.749
- centroid_shift avg down from 0.017 -> 0.012
- cosine_tail (cos<0.95) mass: fp16 zh=3.1%, int6-perchannel zh=4.5% (was 6.8%)

ravi: better but still gap. Try two things: 1) language-specific centering (subtract lang mean) before L2 norm at index time, 2) reindex HNSW with ef_construction=200 and ef_search=150 for zh/pt to test search robustness.

marie: ran lang-mean centering on zh only: zh @10 improved from 0.723 -> 0.736, centroid_shift down another 0.002. Reindex ef_construction=200 helped +0.003.

leo: ensemble note: did you compare avg->quant vs quant->avg for multilingual ckpt ensembles? Sometimes averaging before quant stabilizes rarer-language dims.

marie: tried average-then-quant on three checkpoints: zh @10 = 0.742 vs quant->avg = 0.731. So avg->quant helpful for zh.

mlbot: job 12011 completed: artifacts -> s3://redwood-evals/polyglot/v1/onboard/1766543210/job-12011/

infra-bot: infra parity: staging uses onnxrt 1.15 with GPU fp16 fallback path; prod will use 1.16. Marie: ensure next run on prod image to verify differences.

marie: scheduling prod-run with onnxrt 1.16. Also opened ticket to add per-language calibration as opt-in in onboarding checklist if lang-specific gap > 1.5% @10.

ravi: long-term idea: learn a small per-lang affine (scale+shift) on calibration set to map quant -> fp16 statistics. Cheap at index time and preserves geometry. Test generalization across heldout domains.

marie: will prototype per-lang affine and test across news/forum/docs holdouts. Plan timeline: prod-run + per-lang affine prototyping + 2-week rolling stability check. Will PR docs if stable.

leo: nice. Please include minimal scripts for calibration and a sample command for avg->quant ensemble in the repo.

marie: will do. Linking artifacts and plots in onboarding ticket when prod run completes. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
